input.strategy_title: Bundle an S3-compatible object store for disconnected installs
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Pipelines and model serving both require S3-compatible object storage, but
disconnected customers frequently have none. Field teams work around this by
installing upstream MinIO ad hoc — unsupported, unpatched, and invisible to the
platform. We want a supported, bundled S3-compatible store that administrators
can enable for disconnected and PoC clusters. The leading candidate, MinIO, is
AGPL-3.0 licensed; redistribution terms must be cleared before any productization
work can ship, and the outcome may force a different upstream.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Legal review of redistributing the candidate object store (MinIO, AGPL-3.0) is completed and documented, including the derivative-work posture for operator integration. This clearance blocks all shipping work. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Administrators can enable a supported, bundled S3-compatible object store through the Platform Operator, with productized images and upgrade lifecycle. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Data Science Pipelines and model serving connection defaults can target the bundled store without manual endpoint configuration. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers enablement, sizing guidance, and the supported/unsupported boundary versus customer-provided storage. |

## Affected Components

- Platform Operator
- Data Science Pipelines
- Dashboard
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Replacing customer-provided S3 in connected environments
- Data migration tooling between stores

## Open Questions

1. If AGPL terms cannot be satisfied for our distribution model, the fallback
   candidate is an Apache-2.0 alternative (e.g. SeaweedFS) — acceptable, but it
   restarts image productization.

# Legal clearance for redistributing an AGPL-3.0 S3-compatible object store

## Description

Resolves whether MinIO (AGPL-3.0) can be redistributed as a bundled, supported
component of the platform — including the derivative-work posture for operator
integration — and documents the decision. If the terms cannot be satisfied for
our distribution model, the investigation confirms the Apache-2.0 fallback
candidate (e.g. SeaweedFS) as the replacement upstream and records that image
productization work must restart against it. This clearance blocks all
shipping work in the strategy.

## Scope

- Legal review of redistributing MinIO under AGPL-3.0 in the product's
  distribution model (including disconnected/install-media redistribution)
- Determination of the derivative-work posture for integrating the store with
  the Platform Operator (bundling, deploy, and lifecycle management)
- A documented clearance decision, including any conditions imposed
- If clearance is denied: confirmation of the fallback candidate and a
  statement of the restart impact on image productization

## Questions to Resolve

1. Can MinIO (AGPL-3.0) be redistributed in our distribution model for
   disconnected installs?
2. Does Platform Operator integration (bundling, deployment, upgrade
   management) create a derivative work under AGPL-3.0, and if so, can the
   posture be made acceptable?
3. If the terms cannot be satisfied: is the Apache-2.0 fallback candidate
   (e.g. SeaweedFS) confirmed as the replacement upstream?

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the legal review of AGPL-3.0 redistribution terms, When the review
  completes, Then the clearance decision — including the derivative-work
  posture for operator integration — is documented and accessible to all
  downstream teams.
- Measured by: a written clearance decision exists; either redistribution is
  cleared (possibly with conditions) or the fallback upstream is confirmed
  with the restart of image productization planned.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): Legal review of redistributing the candidate object store
  (MinIO, AGPL-3.0) completed and documented, including the derivative-work
  posture for operator integration.

# Midstream repo onboarding for the bundled object store

## Description

Creates the midstream repository for the legally cleared S3-compatible object
store candidate under opendatahub-io, establishing the fork point and repo
conventions needed to productize the store's container image. This replaces
the current unsupported field practice of installing upstream MinIO ad hoc.

## Scope

- Midstream repository creation for the cleared object store candidate under
  opendatahub-io
- Initial import of the selected upstream release
- Repo configuration consistent with other opendatahub-io midstream component
  repos (branch conventions, maintainers, README)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the legal clearance decision, When the midstream repository is
  created, Then it contains the cleared candidate's source at the selected
  upstream release and follows opendatahub-io midstream repo conventions.
- The repository is ready for build-pipeline onboarding; no pipeline
  configuration is delivered in this epic.
- Measured by: the repository exists under opendatahub-io with the imported
  release and standard repo conventions.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): Administrators can enable a supported, bundled S3-compatible
  object store — this epic provides the repo foundation for productized
  images.

# License validation for the bundled object store

## Description

Runs license scanning over the cleared object store candidate and its full
transitive dependency tree to produce the license evidence for the productized
image, surfacing any problematic transitive dependencies beyond the headline
AGPL redistribution question. This complements (and runs after) the legal
clearance decision: clearance settles the store's own license; this epic
verifies the dependencies behind it.

## Scope

- License scan of the cleared candidate's source and complete transitive
  dependency tree
- License report for the productized image
- Escalation of findings that conflict with the documented redistribution
  posture (e.g. copyleft transitive dependencies)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the cleared candidate, When license scanning completes, Then a license
  report covering the full transitive dependency tree of the productized image
  is produced.
- Any blocking license findings are escalated and resolved before the operator
  enablement work proceeds.
- Measured by: scan report delivered; no unresolved blocking license findings
  against the redistribution posture.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): documents the licensing posture of the redistributed store and
  its dependencies.
- HLR-2 (P0): supported, productized images require clean license evidence.

# Platform Operator enablement of the bundled S3-compatible object store

## Description

Delivers administrator-facing enablement of the bundled S3-compatible object
store through the Platform Operator: deploying the productized store image
under the platform's upgrade lifecycle, so administrators of disconnected and
PoC clusters can run a supported store instead of unsupported ad hoc upstream
installs.

## Scope

- Operator-managed deployment of the productized object store image
- Administrator opt-in enablement of the bundled store (targeting disconnected
  and PoC clusters; customer-provided S3 in connected environments remains the
  default and out of scope)
- Upgrade lifecycle integration so image updates for the bundled store flow
  through the operator's upgrade path
- The bundled store is visible to the platform (inventoried and managed) rather
  than an invisible field workaround

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the productized store image and its midstream repository, When an
  administrator enables the bundled store through the Platform Operator, Then
  a supported S3-compatible object store runs on the cluster and is managed
  through the platform upgrade lifecycle.
- The store's build pipeline is green (the image is built through the standard
  Konflux pipeline, not a one-off build).
- Enabling or not enabling the bundled store does not alter behavior of
  customer-provided S3 configurations.
- Measured by: an administrator can enable and use the bundled store on a
  disconnected cluster without manually installing upstream software.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): Administrators can enable a supported, bundled S3-compatible
  object store through the Platform Operator, with productized images and
  upgrade lifecycle.

# Data Science Pipelines connection defaults for the bundled store

## Description

Updates Data Science Pipelines so artifact storage connection defaults target
the bundled S3-compatible object store on clusters where it is enabled,
without manual endpoint configuration. Data Science Pipelines already depends
on S3-compatible object storage for artifacts; this work removes the manual
endpoint setup step when the platform-provided store is present.

## Scope

- Default artifact storage connection targeting the bundled store when it is
  enabled on the cluster
- No manual endpoint configuration required when the bundled store is present
- Clusters using customer-provided S3 continue to work unchanged

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a cluster with the bundled store enabled, When a Data Science
  Pipelines application is created, Then its artifact storage connection
  defaults to the bundled store with no manual endpoint configuration.
- Explicitly configured customer-provided storage continues to be honored.
- Measured by: pipeline runs on a disconnected cluster store artifacts in the
  bundled store with zero endpoint configuration.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): Data Science Pipelines connection defaults can target the
  bundled store without manual endpoint configuration.
